links.outcome: Adequacy of chatbot responses to simulated escalating suicidal risk scenarios (C-SSRS-based prompts)
links.effect: None of 29 agents met the adequate-response criteria; 51.72% gave marginal responses and 48.28% were inadequate. Common errors: no emergency contact information and lack of contextual understanding.
links.quote: None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate.

links.outcome: Recognition and escalation of suicidal crisis in escalating simulated chatbot scenarios
links.effect: No agent gave an adequate response; 48.28% were inadequate. Common errors included failure to provide emergency contact information and poor contextual understanding.
links.quote: Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding.

screen.reason: Evaluated the performance and safety of 29 commercial mental health chatbot agents in handling simulated suicidal crisis scenarios, finding significant deficiencies in crisis escalation/referral.
